title: fix(proxy): keep WebChat and Codex loopback calls direct
body:
Closes #153930. Thanks @eefreenyc for the report and proxy-environment comparison.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WebChat/native Codex loopback 502 and handshake failures after upgrading a managed-proxy installation from 9.3 to 9.4/9.5.

## User Impact

Default managed routing keeps runtime loopback HTTP/WebSocket listeners direct while external requests still use the proxy. Explicit `proxy` and `block` modes remain enforced. Doctor reports failed loopback probes with recovery commands, and update-readiness diagnostics identify the route correctly. No new configuration option or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commit `8169aacdda92`, first shipped in 9.4, added a native Codex loopback inference relay while managed routing still cleared `NO_PROXY`. The shared Proxyline bypass policy and loopback exclusions for native children repair that boundary. Per-request registrations are no longer needed; retained callbacks still enforce explicit block policy.

The CI follow-up preserves that routing contract. Main's wildcard-listener change `192ff574a21` concerns TCP readiness, and `7723e490386` concerns Doctor completion/cleanup; neither calls for sending default loopback traffic through an external proxy.

## Evidence

CI attached to head `e5310014ee9386015eb0ea896d0c5975cfc9f8f6`: [run 35557127865](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35557127865), in progress at handoff.

Input-safety fixture follow-up: replaced the Doctor test proxy URL containing username/password userinfo with an unauthenticated reserved `.test` URL. Production code and assertions are unchanged. All **17 Doctor tests passed**, with a longest case of **148 ms**; local wrapper wall time was **195.80 s**, including **116.886 s** preparing the shared subprocess bundle (11,195 inputs / 15,060 outputs). The initial local build could not execute tests because the pre-rebase install had fs-safe 0.16.0; restoring the existing frozen lockfile installed the declared 0.17.0 without source/lockfile edits. Scoped formatting, lint, and fresh P1 autoreview passed. Exactly one re-review request was posted for this revision.

Testbox proof: [owned Linux runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35547270341). All **197 focused tests passed**. The four original CI shard selections each passed **three replays in their original order**, totaling **15,822 passing cases per replay**. TUI and outbound-custody files each passed **20/20** standalone reliability runs after fixing their causes. The new direct-probe diagnostic regression was also demonstrated failing against the original readiness implementation.

Final `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` completed with **exit 0**, including core/test typechecks, formatting, lint, guards, and all three dead-export scans. The first gate caught the TUI fixture's unsupported `Promise.withResolvers`; replacing it with the existing `createDeferred` helper was followed by a fresh TUI run (**18 passed**) and the complete green gate. Fresh P1 autoreview: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable P0 or P1 findings. The owned Testbox is stopped; its wrapper's successful exit/timing evidence is authoritative if lease cleanup marks the Actions container run cancelled.

Measured focused-file wall time with one worker on Testbox:

| File | Passing tests | Wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/tui/gateway-chat.test.ts` (final corrected run) | 18 | 11.52 s |
| `src/infra/update-candidate-canary.test.ts` | 53 | 19.92 s |
| `src/gateway/client.test.ts` | 116 | 13.05 s |
| `src/infra/state-migrations.outbound-custody.test.ts` | 4 | 8.11 s, versus the original 90 s setup timeout |
| `src/infra/state-migrations.outbound-preparation.test.ts` | 6 | 21.04 s |

The test interdiff is **+143/−101 lines** (net +42); the production interdiff is detailed below.

| Failing file | Decision and repair |
| --- | --- |
| `src/tui/gateway-chat.test.ts` | **(a) Fixture/assertion update.** A preceding module reset split client and proxy ownership, causing Proxyline to reject different callback identities before the block guard. Import both from the same module graph, await error delivery, and assert the full block error plus recovery command exactly once. |
| `src/infra/update-candidate-canary.test.ts` | **(a) Contract update.** The live loopback listener must still return 200 after readiness under the persistent default bypass; the external target must return the dummy proxy's 502. Request accounting is exact, and explicit proxy/block cases remain. A new regression also prevents labeling a failed direct probe as “via proxy.” |
| `src/gateway/client.test.ts` | **(a) Contract update.** Replace retired registration/unregistration counts with the installed policy's loopback/external decisions before WebSocket construction, retaining exact connection-error forwarding and proxy/block tests. Restore all environment fields changed by inherited routing. |
| `src/infra/state-migrations.outbound-custody.test.ts` | **Existing owner repair, #154123 (`c159663b126`).** The 90-second failure came from a fixture running four broad Doctor sweeps. Reuse the focused nested-maintenance test repair, preserving native writability, physical exclusion, exact acquisition/disposal causes, and receipt coverage. Deadlines are unchanged. |

The production interdiff against `630e6f50dd9` is **+6/−2 lines**, solely in `src/infra/update-candidate-canary-readiness.ts`: proxy attribution now comes from the effective mode rather than the removed registration's return value. No routing-policy narrowing was needed.

Initial proof remains: 75 focused tests, routing and Doctor regressions demonstrated failing before the fix, and an isolated real-Gateway/native-Codex turn completed in 15.144 seconds with zero loopback proxy attempts and four external proxy connections to a scripted provider. Cleanup confirmed the owned Gateway stopped.

**Known separate defect:** the first isolated attempt spent **70.3 s** reaching Gateway readiness, then failed with `codex app-server request timed out`. Native model discovery applies its **2.5 s acquisition budget** at [`extensions/codex/src/app-server/model-catalog.ts:126`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bc041becd3fa0c1177dc821f5dc56efe3c467acd/extensions/codex/src/app-server/model-catalog.ts#L126); the timed scope in [`request.ts:308`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bc041becd3fa0c1177dc821f5dc56efe3c467acd/extensions/codex/src/app-server/request.ts#L308) includes app-server preparation and startup before catalog reads. The exact expired phase was not captured. This is assigned to a separate native-startup budget repair lane; the successful instrumented turn is proxy-routing evidence, not a repair of that timeout.

## Landing review disposition

The latest ClawSweeper comment (5752252448, updated 2026-09-21 02:20:59 UTC) reports that its input-safety check blocked review; it contains no completed verdict or Rank-up moves. There are therefore no Rank-up changes to apply or skip. The native ClawSweeper gate reports `completed review is missing or expired`, so landing is stopped pending maintainer qualification of the flagged material and a completed review. This does not assert that the material is a real credential or a safe fixture. No source changes or test reruns were made during this landing attempt.
